title: Bhangui
steps: Mix rice with grated ginger, onion, turmeric and a little mustard oil or ghee.
Wrap in banana leaves, forming conical or packet shapes, and steam until the rice is cooked and infused with the leaf aroma.
Serve hot – a fragrant traditional rice preparation.

fullIngredients.name: Ginger, onion, turmeric, mustard oil or ghee

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The banana leaf imparts a unique aroma and keeps the rice moist.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often eaten as a light meal or breakfast.

title: Steamed Rice with Mosdeng Serma
steps: Steam or boil rice. Separately pound or grind berma with red chilli, garlic and tomato into a spicy, pungent chutney (mosdeng serma).
Serve the rice with the mosdeng as a simple, flavourful start to the day.

fullIngredients.name: Berma (fermented dried fish), red chilli, garlic, tomato

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mosdeng is the classic Tripuri side – fiery, umami-rich and essential to most meals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Berma gives the distinctive fermented flavour.

title: Gudok
steps: Boil the vegetables with berma, chilli and salt until soft. Mash everything together into a thick, flavourful mixture.
Garnish with sliced onion. Serve with steamed rice – a staple tribal dish cooked with little or no oil.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal vegetables (potato, beans, pumpkin, bamboo shoot, etc.)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional oil-free preparation – the fermented fish provides the main flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Vegetables vary with season and availability.

title: Mui Borok
steps: Layer or combine vegetables, bamboo shoot and berma with aromatics. Boil or steam until everything is soft and the flavours have melded.
Mash lightly if desired. Serve with rice – often called the soul food of Tripura.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal vegetables, bamboo shoot, bottle gourd
Ginger leaves, onion, garlic, green chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mui Borok is considered the traditional cuisine of the Tripuri people.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Minimal oil, maximum use of local produce and fermented fish.

title: Chakhwi
steps: Cook bamboo shoot and other vegetables with a little alkaline water (traditionally extracted from burnt plant ash) and rice paste to thicken.
Season with onion, garlic, chilli and salt. Simmer into a light stew.
Serve with rice – a distinctive Tripuri preparation.

fullIngredients.name: Bamboo shoot, banana stem, papaya, other vegetables
Rice paste, alkaline water (khar) or soda, onion, garlic, chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The mild alkaline note is characteristic of traditional Chakhwi.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Bamboo shoot is central.

title: Wahan Mosdeng
steps: Marinate pork with garlic, ginger, chilli and a little mustard oil. Grill, roast or pan-cook until done.
Chop or shred and mix with more fresh chilli, onion and aromatics into a spicy salad-style preparation (mosdeng).
Serve with rice or roti.

fullIngredients.name: Garlic, ginger, green chilli, onion, mustard oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Pork salad/bharta – bold, spicy and very popular.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Can also be made with chicken.

title: Mach Bhat (Fish Curry with Rice)
steps: Marinate fish with turmeric and salt. Lightly fry or cook in a simple gravy of onion, ginger, garlic, chilli and mustard oil.
Serve with steamed rice – the everyday fish-and-rice meal of the region.

fullIngredients.name: Turmeric, mustard oil, green chilli, onion, ginger, garlic

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Fish and rice form the cornerstone of daily Tripura diet.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil is commonly used.

title: Mwkhwi (Fruit Snack)
steps: Cut fresh seasonal fruit into pieces. Toss with salt and crushed green chilli.
Eat as a refreshing, spicy-sweet snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple fruit preparation popular when mangoes, pineapples or other local fruits are in season.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The chilli-salt combination is classic.

title: Mosdeng (Bamboo Shoot Chutney)
steps: Pound or grind bamboo shoot with chilli, garlic and salt into a coarse chutney.
Mix in chopped onion. Serve as a side or snack with rice cakes or puffed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Red or green chilli, garlic, onion, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mosdeng variations are endless – bamboo shoot versions are especially popular.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Pungent and addictive.

title: Awandru (Vegetarian Bamboo Shoot Gravy)
steps: Cook bamboo shoot with onion, garlic, chilli and rice flour into a light gravy.
Simmer till the flavours blend. Garnish with fresh herbs.
Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, garlic, chilli, salt, coriander for garnish

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Vegetarian bamboo-shoot based gravy common in Tripuri cooking.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Thickened with rice flour instead of fish.

title: Awandru with Berma (Non-Vegetarian)
steps: Cook bamboo shoot with berma, onion and chilli into a light gravy.
Simmer till the flavours blend. Garnish with fresh herbs.
Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, chilli, salt, coriander for garnish

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional non-vegetarian bamboo-shoot gravy thickened with berma.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The fermented fish adds a deep, umami richness.

title: Pork with Bamboo Shoot
steps: Cook pork with ginger, garlic, onion and chilli until tender. Add bamboo shoot and continue cooking till the flavours meld.
Serve with steamed rice – a hearty tribal favourite.

fullIngredients.name: Green chilli, ginger, garlic, onion, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Bamboo shoot cuts through the richness of the pork.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Fermented bamboo shoot adds extra tang.

title: Khoi / Puffed Rice Snack
steps: Toss puffed rice with a little mustard oil, chopped onion, green chilli and salt.
Eat immediately as a light, crunchy snack.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil, onion, green chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple everyday snack across the region.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Can be dressed up with more vegetables or berma for extra flavour.
